Some items, like bows and shields, do not have a limit to their use. They will return 1 hour.

5061.name: Attacker
5061.desc:
The attacker of a damage event, e.g. when a player attacks a zombie this expression represents the player.
Please note that the attacker can also be a block, e.g. a cactus or lava, but this expression will not be set in these cases.

10949.name: Middle of Location
10949.desc: Returns the middle/center of a location. In other words, returns the middle of the X, Z coordinates and the floor value of the Y coordinate of a location.

5062.name: Bed
5062.desc: The bed location of a player, i.e. the spawn point of a player if he ever slept in a bed and the bed still exists and is unobstructed.

5318.name: Inventory
5318.desc:
An inventory of a player or block. Inventories have many effects and conditions regarding the items contained.
An inventory has a fixed amount of slots which represent a specific place in the inventory, e.g. the helmet slot for players (Please note that slot support is still very limited but will be improved eventually).

5063.name: Biome
5063.desc: The biome at a certain location. Please note that biomes are only defined for x/z-columns, i.e. the altitude (y-coordinate) doesn't matter.

5319.name: Inventory Action
5319.desc: What player just did in inventory event. Note that when in creative game mode, most actions do not work correctly.

4808.name: On Enchant
4808.desc:
Called when a player successfully enchants an item.
 To get the enchanted item, see the enchant item expression

5064.name: Block
5064.desc:
The block involved in the event, e.g. the clicked block or the placed block.
Can optionally include a direction as well, e.g. 'block above' or 'block in front of the player'.

5320.name: Inventory Slot
5320.desc:
Represents a single slot of an inventory. Notable slots are the armour slots and furnace slots. 
The most important property that distinguishes a slot from an item is its ability to be changed, e.g. it can be set, deleted, enchanted, etc. (Some item expressions can be changed as well, e.g. items stored in variables. For that matter: slots are never saved to variables, only the items they represent at the time when the variable is set).
Please note that tool can be regarded a slot, but it can actually change it's position, i.e. doesn't represent always the same slot.

10952.name: View Distance
10952.desc:
The view distance of a player as set by the server. Can be changed.
NOTE: This is the view distance sent by the server to the player.
This has nothing to do with client side view distance settings
NOTE: This may not work on some versions (such as MC 1.14.x).
The return value in this case will be the view distance set in system.properties.

4809.name: On Enchant Prepare
4809.desc:
Called when a player puts an item into enchantment table. This event may be called multiple times.
 To get the enchant item, see the enchant item expression

10953.name: Portal Cooldown
10953.desc:
The amount of time before an entity can use a portal. By default, it is 15 seconds after exiting a nether portal or end gateway.
Players in survival/adventure get a cooldown of 0.5 seconds, while those in creative get no cooldown.
Resetting will set the cooldown back to the default 15 seconds for non-player entities and 0.5 seconds for players.

4810.name: On Enderman/Sheep/Silverfish
4810.desc: Called when an enderman places or picks up a block, a sheep eats grass or a silverfish boops into/out of a block respectively.
4810.pattern:
[on] enderman place
[on] enderman pickup
[on] sheep eat
[on] silverfish enter
[on] silverfish exit

5322.name: Item / Material
5322.desc:
An item, e.g. a stack of torches, a furnace, or a wooden sword of sharpness 2. Unlike item type an item can only represent exactly one item (e.g. an upside-down cobblestone stair facing west), while an item type can represent a whole range of items (e.g. any cobble stone stairs regardless of direction).
You don't usually need this type except when you want to make a command that only accepts an exact item.
Please note that currently 'material' is exactly the same as 'item', i.e. can have an amount & enchantments.

5067.name: Blocks
5067.desc:
Blocks relative to other blocks or between other blocks. Can be used to get blocks relative to other blocks or for looping.
Blocks from/to and between will return a straight line whereas blocks within will return a cuboid.
5067.pattern:
[(all [[of] the]|the)] blocks %direction% [%locations%]
[(all [[of] the]|the)] blocks from %location% [on] %direction%
[(all [[of] the]|the)] blocks from %location% to %location%
[(all [[of] the]|the)] blocks between %location% and %location%
[(all [[of] the]|the)] blocks within %location% and %location%
[(all [[of] the]|the)] blocks (in|within) %chunk%
5067.changers:
add
set
remove
remove all
delete

5323.name: Item Type
5323.desc:
An item type is an alias, e.g. 'a pickaxe', 'all plants', etc., and can result in different items when added to an inventory, and unlike items they are well suited for checking whether an inventory contains a certain item or whether a certain item is of a certain type.
An item type can also have one or more enchantments with or without a specific level defined, and can optionally start with 'all' or 'every' to make this item type represent all types that the alias represents, including data ranges.

10956.name: Total Experience
10956.desc:
The total experience, in points, of players or experience orbs.
Adding to a player's experience will trigger Mending, but setting their experience will not.

4813.name: On Experience Spawn
4813.desc:
Called whenever experience is about to spawn. This is a helper event for easily being able to stop xp from spawning, as all you can currently do is cancel the event.
Please note that it's impossible to detect xp orbs spawned by plugins (including Skript) with Bukkit, thus make sure that you have no such plugins if you don't want any xp orbs to spawn. (Many plugins that only change the experience dropped by blocks or entities will be detected without problems though)

5325.name: Location
5325.desc: A location in a world. Locations are world-specific and even store a direction, e.g. if you save a location and later teleport to it you will face the exact same direction you did when you saved the location.

4815.name: On Explosion Prime
4815.desc: Called when an explosive is primed, i.e. an entity will explode shortly. Creepers can abort the explosion if the player gets too far away, while TNT will explode for sure after a short time.

5327.name: Money
5327.desc: A certain amount of money. Please note that this differs from numbers as it includes a currency symbol or name, but usually the two are interchangeable, e.g. you can both add 100$ to the player's balance and add 100 to the player's balance.

10959.name: On Inventory Item Move
10959.desc:
Called when an entity or block (e.g. hopper) tries to move items directly from one inventory to another.
When this event is called, the initiator may have already removed the item from the source inventory and is ready to move it into the destination inventory.
If this event is cancelled, the items will be returned to the source inventory.

5072.name: Burn/Cook Time
5072.desc:
The time a furnace takes to burn an item in a fuel burn event.
Can also be used to change the burn/cook time of a placed furnace.

5328.name: Number
5328.desc:
A number, e.g. 2.5, 3, or -9812454.
Please note that many expressions only need integers, i.e. will discard any fractional parts of any numbers without producing an error.

5329.name: Object
5329.desc: The supertype of all types, meaning that if %object% is used in e.g. a condition it will accept all kinds of expressions.

10961.name: On Move / Rotate
10961.desc:
Called when a player or entity moves or rotates their head.
NOTE: Move event will only be called when the entity/player moves position, keyword 'turn around' is for orientation (ie: looking around), and the combined syntax listens for both.
NOTE: These events can be performance heavy as they are called quite often.

5074.name: Chat Format
5074.desc: Can be used to get/retrieve the chat format. The sender of a message is represented by [player] or [sender], and the message by [message] or [msg].

5330.name: Offline Player
5330.desc: A player that is possibly offline. See player for more information. Please note that while all effects and conditions that require a player can be used with an offline player as well, they will not work if the player is not actually online.

10962.name: On Move On
10962.desc:
Called when a player moves onto a certain type of block.
Please note that using this event can cause lag if there are many players online.

5331.name: Player
5331.desc:
A player. Depending on whether a player is online or offline several actions can be performed with them, though you won't get any errors when using effects that only work if the player is online (e.g. changing their inventory) on an offline player.
You have two possibilities to use players as command arguments: <player> and <offline player>. The first requires that the player is online and also accepts only part of the name, while the latter doesn't require that the player is online, but the player's name has to be entered exactly.

10963.name: On Player Chunk Enter
10963.desc: Called when a player enters a chunk. Note that this event is based on 'player move' event, and may be called frequent internally.

4821.name: On Flow
4821.desc: Called when a blocks flows or teleports to another block. This not only applies to water and lava, but teleporting dragon eggs as well.

10965.name: On Egg Throw
10965.desc: Called when a player throws an egg and it lands. You can just use the shoot in most cases. However, this event allows modification of properties like the hatched entity type and the number of entities to hatch.

4822.name: On Form
4822.desc: Called when a block is created, but not by a player, e.g. snow forms due to snowfall, water freezes in cold biomes. This isn't called when block spreads (mushroom growth, water physics etc.), as it has its own event (see spread event).

5078.name: Colour of
5078.desc: The colour of an item, can also be used to colour chat messages with "<%colour of ...%>this text is coloured!".

5334.name: Region
5334.desc:
A region of a regions plugin. Skript currently supports WorldGuard, Factions, GriefPrevention and PreciousStones.
Please note that some regions plugins do not have named regions, some use numerical ids to identify regions, and some may have regions with the same name in different worlds, thus using regions like "region name" in scripts may or may not work.

10966.name: On Anvil Prepare
10966.desc: Called when an item is put in a slot for repair by an anvil. Please note that this event is called multiple times in a single item slot move.

5079.name: Coloured / Uncoloured
5079.desc: Parses <colour>s and, optionally, chat styles in a message or removes", "any colours <i>and</i> chat styles from the message. Parsing all", "chat styles requires this expression to be used in same line with", "the <a href=effects.html#EffSend>send effect</a>.

4825.name: On Gliding State Change
4825.desc: Called when an entity toggles glider on or off, or when server toggles gliding state of an entity forcibly.

5081.name: Command Sender
5081.desc:
The player or the console who sent a command. Mostly useful in commands and command events.
If the command sender is a command block, its location can be retrieved by using %block's location%

5337.name: Sound Category
5337.desc: The category of a sound, they are used for sound options of Minecraft. See the play sound and stop sound effects.

10969.name: On Anvil Damage
10969.desc:
Called when an anvil is damaged/broken from being used to repair/rename items.
Note: this does not include anvil damage from falling.

10970.name: On Stop Using Item
10970.desc:
Called when a player stops using an item. For example, when the player releases the interact button when holding a bow, an edible item, or a spyglass.
Note that event-timespan will return the time the item was used for.

10971.name: On Ready Arrow
10971.desc:
Called when a player is firing a bow and the server is choosing an arrow to use.
Cancelling this event will skip the current arrow item and fire a new event for the next arrow item.
The arrow and bow in the event can be accessed with the Readied Arrow/Bow expression.

4828.name: On Heal
4828.desc: Called when an entity is healed, e.g. by eating (players), being fed (pets), or by the effect of a potion of healing (overworld mobs) or harm (nether mobs).

5084.name: Cooldown Time/Remaining Time/Elapsed Time/Last Usage/Bypass Permission
5084.desc: Only usable in command events. Represents the cooldown time, the remaining time, the elapsed time,", "the last usage date, or the cooldown bypass permission.
5084.pattern:
[the] remaining [time] [of [the] (cooldown|wait) [(of|for) [the] [current] command]]
[the] elapsed [time] [of [the] (cooldown|wait) [(of|for) [the] [current] command]]
[the] ((cooldown|wait) time|[wait] time of [the] (cooldown|wait) [(of|for) [the] [current] command])
[the] last usage [date] [of [the] (cooldown|wait) [(of|for) [the] [current] command]]
[the] [cooldown] bypass perm[ission] [of [the] (cooldown|wait) [(of|for) [the] [current] command]]

5340.name: Text
5340.desc:
Text is simply text, i.e. a sequence of characters, which can optionally contain expressions which will be replaced with a meaningful representation (e.g. %player% will be replaced with the player's name).
Because scripts are also text, you have to put text into double quotes to tell Skript which part of the line is an effect/expression and which part is the text.
Please read the article on Texts and Variable Names to learn more.

10972.name: On Inventory Slot Change
10972.desc:
Called when a slot in a player's inventory is changed.
Warning: setting the event-slot to a new item can result in an infinite loop.

5341.name: Time
5341.desc:
A time is a point in a minecraft day's time (i.e. ranges from 0:00 to 23:59), which can vary per world.
See date and timespan for the other time types of Skript.

10973.name: On Loot Generate
10973.desc:
Called when a loot table of an inventory is generated in the world.
For example, when opening a shipwreck chest.

4830.name: On Hunger Meter Change
4830.desc: Called when the hunger bar of a player changes, i.e. either increases by eating or decreases over time.

5086.name: Creature/Entity/Player/Projectile/Villager/Powered Creeper/etc.
5086.desc:
The entity involved in an event (an entity is a player, a creature or an inanimate object like ignited TNT, a dropped item or an arrow).
You can use the specific type of the entity that's involved in the event, e.g. in a 'death of a creeper' event you can use 'the creeper' instead of 'the entity'.

5342.name: Timeperiod
5342.desc:
A period of time between two times. Mostly useful since you can use this to test for whether it's day, night, dusk or dawn in a specific world.
This type might be removed in the future as you can use 'time of world is between x and y' as a replacement.

7646.name: Hostname
7646.desc: The hostname used by the connecting player to connect to the server in a <a href='events.html#connect'>connect</a> event.

10974.name: On Player Deep Sleep
10974.desc:
Called when a player has slept long enough to count as passing the night/storm.
Cancelling this event will prevent the player from being counted as deeply sleeping unless they exit and re-enter the bed.

4831.name: On Ignition
4831.desc:
Called when a block starts burning, i.e. a fire block is placed next to it and this block is flammable.
The burn event will be called when the block is about do be destroyed by the fire.

5087.name: Cursor Slot
5087.desc: The item which the player has on their cursor. This slot is always empty if player has no inventories open.
5087.changers:
add
set
remove
remove all
delete

5343.name: Timespan
5343.desc:
A timespan is a difference of two different dates or times, e.g '10 minutes'. Timespans are always displayed as real life time, but can be defined as minecraft time, e.g. '5 minecraft days and 12 hours'.
See date and time for the other time types of Skript.

5088.name: Custom Chest Inventory
5088.desc: Returns a chest inventory with the given amount of rows and the name. Use the <a href=effects.html#EffOpenInventory>open inventory</a> effect to open it.
5088.pattern:
[a [new]] chest inventory (named|with name) %string% [with %-number% row[s]]
[a [new]] chest inventory with %number% row[s] [(named|with name) %-string%]

5344.name: Tree Type
5344.desc: A tree type represents a tree species or a huge mushroom species. These can be generated in a world with the generate tree effect.

5345.name: Type
5345.desc:
Represents a type, e.g. number, object, item type, location, block, world, entity type, etc.
This is mostly used for expressions like 'event-<type>', '<type>-argument', 'loop-<type>', etc., e.g. event-world, number-argument and loop-player.

5090.name: Damage
5090.desc: How much damage is done in a damage event, possibly ignoring armour, criticals and/or enchantments. Can be changed (remember that in Skript '1' is one full heart, not half a heart).

5346.name: Vector
5346.desc: Vector is a collection of numbers. In Minecraft, 3D vectors are used to express velocities of entities.

4836.name: On Item Break
4836.desc:
Called when a player breaks their tool because its damage reached the maximum value.
This event cannot be cancelled.

5092.name: Damaged Item
5092.desc: Directly damages an item. In MC versions 1.12.2 and lower, this can be used to apply data values to items/blocks

10980.name: offlineplayer
10980.desc: Returns a offline player from their name or UUID. This function will still return the player if they're online.

4837.name: On Item Damage
4837.desc: Called when an item is damaged. Most tools are damaged by using them; armor is damaged when the wearer takes damage.

5093.name: Data/Damage Value
5093.desc:
The data/damage value of an item/block. Data values of blocks are only supported on 1.12.2 and below.
You usually don't need this expression as you can check and set items with aliases easily, 
but this expression can e.g. be used to "add 1 to data of <item>", e.g. for cycling through all wool colours.

5349.name: World
5349.desc: One of the server's worlds. Worlds can be put into scripts by surrounding their name with double quotes, e.g. "world_nether", but this might not work reliably as text uses the same syntax.

4838.name: On Item Despawn
4838.desc: Called when an item is about to be despawned from the world, usually 5 minutes after it was dropped.

10982.name: player
10982.desc:
Returns an online player from their name or UUID, if player is offline function will return nothing.
Setting 'getExactPlayer' parameter to true will return the player whose name is exactly equal to the provided name instead of returning a player that their name starts with the provided name.

5095.name: Default Value
5095.desc: A shorthand expression for giving things a default value. If the first thing isn't set, the second thing will be returned.

4841.name: On Item Spawn
4841.desc: Called whenever an item stack is spawned in a world, e.g. as drop of a block or mob, a player throwing items out of their inventory, or a dispenser dispensing an item (not shooting it).

4842.name: On Join
4842.desc: Called when the player joins the server. The player is already in a world when this event is called, so if you want to prevent players from joining you should prefer on connect over this event.

4844.name: On Kick
4844.desc: Called when a player is kicked from the server. You can change the kick message or cancel the event entirely.

5100.name: Drops
5100.desc: Only works in death events. Holds the drops of the dying creature. Drops can be prevented by removing them with "remove ... from drops", e.g. "remove all pickaxes from the drops", or "clear drops" if you don't want any drops at all.

4845.name: On Language Change
4845.desc:
Called after a player changed their language in the game settings. You can use the language expression to get the current language of the player.
This event requires Minecraft 1.12+.

5103.name: Enchant Item
5103.desc:
The enchant item in an enchant prepare event or enchant event.
It can be modified, but enchantments will still be applied in the enchant event.

5104.name: Enchanting Experience Cost
5104.desc: The cost of enchanting in an enchant event.", "This is number that was displayed in the enchantment table, not the actual number of levels removed.

4849.name: On Step/Walk On
4849.desc: Called when a player moves onto a certain type of block. Please note that using this event can cause lag if there are many players online.

5105.name: Enchantment Bonus
5105.desc: The enchantment bonus in an enchant prepare event. This represents the number of bookshelves affecting/surrounding the enchantment table.

4850.name: On Physics
4850.desc: Called when a physics check is done on a block. By cancelling this event you can prevent some things from happening, e.g. sand falling, dirt turning into grass, torches dropping if their supporting block is destroyed, etc.Please note that using this event might cause quite some lag since it gets called extremely often.

4851.name: On Pick Up
4851.desc: Called when a player/entity picks up an item. Please note that the item is still on the ground when this event is called.
4851.eventvalues:
event-itementity
event-player
event-world
event-commandsender
event-itemtype
event-entity

4852.name: On Pig Zap
4852.desc: Called when a pig is stroke by lightning and transformed into a zombie pigman. Cancel the event to prevent the transformation.

5108.name: Enchantment Offer Enchantment Cost
5108.desc:
The cost of an enchantment offer. This is displayed to the right of an enchantment offer.
 If the cost is changed, it will always be at least 1.
 This changes how many levels are required to enchant, but does not change the number of levels removed.
 To change the number of levels removed, use the enchant event.

5110.name: Entities
5110.desc: All entities in all worlds, in a specific world, in a chunk or in a radius around a certain location, e.g. 'all players', 'all creepers in the player's world', or 'players in radius 100 of the player'.
5110.pattern:
[(all [[of] the]|the)] %*entitydatas% [(in|of) ([world[s]] %worlds%|%chunks%)]
[(all [[of] the]|the)] entities of type[s] %entitydatas% [(in|of) ([world[s]] %worlds%|%chunks%)]
[(all [[of] the]|the)] %*entitydatas% (within|[with]in radius) %number% [(block[s]|met(er|re)[s])] (of|around) %location%
[(all [[of] the]|the)] entities of type[s] %entitydatas% in radius %number% (of|around) %location%

5112.name: Entity Attribute
5112.desc:
The numerical value of an entity's particular attribute.
Note that the movement speed attribute cannot be reliably used for players. For that purpose, use the speed expression instead.
Resetting an entity's attribute is only available in Minecraft 1.11 and above.

4857.name: On Portal
4857.desc: Called when a player uses a nether or end portal. Cancel the event to prevent the player from teleporting.

4858.name: On Portal Create
4858.desc:
Called when a portal is created, either by a player or mob lighting an obsidian frame on fire, or by a nether portal creating its teleportation target in the nether/overworld.
Please note that it's not possible to use the player in this event.

4860.name: Prepare Craft
4860.desc: Called just before displaying crafting result to player. Note that setting the result item might or might not work due to Bukkit bugs.

5117.name: Explosion Block Yield
5117.desc:
The percentage of exploded blocks dropped in an explosion event.
When changing the yield, a value greater than 1 will function the same as using 1.
Attempting to change the yield to a value less than 0 will have no effect.

5118.name: Explosion Yield
5118.desc:
The yield of the explosion in an explosion prime event. This is how big the explosion is.
 When changing the yield, values less than 0 will be ignored.
 Read this wiki page for more information

4863.name: On Projectile Hit
4863.desc:
Called when a projectile hits an entity or a block.
Use the damage event with a check for a projectile to be able to use the entity that got hit in the case when the projectile hit a living entity.
A damage event will even be fired if the damage is 0, e.g. when throwing snowballs at non-nether mobs.

5119.name: Explosive Yield
5119.desc:
The yield of an explosive (creeper, primed tnt, fireball, etc.). This is how big of an explosion is caused by the entity.
Read this wiki page for more information

4975.name: Cancel Command Cooldown
4975.desc: Only usable in commands. Makes it so the current command usage isn't counted towards the cooldown.

10870.name: Has Line of Sight
10870.desc: Checks whether living entities have an unobstructed line of sight to other entities or locations.
10870.pattern:
%livingentities% (has|have) [a] [direct] line of sight to %entities/locations%
%livingentities% does(n't| not) have [a] [direct] line of sight to %entities/locations%
%livingentities% (has|have) no [direct] line of sight to %entities/locations%

4875.name: On Shoot
4875.desc: Called whenever a projectile is shot. Use the shooter expression to get who shot the projectile.

4885.name: On Swim Toggle
4885.desc: Called when an entity swims or stops swimming.

5167.name: Last Damage
5167.desc: The last damage that was done to an entity. Note that changing it doesn't deal more/less damage.

10615.name: exp
10615.desc: The exponential function. You probably don't need this if you don't know what this is.

5324.name: Living Entity
5324.desc: A living entity, i.e. a mob or player, not inanimate entities like projectiles or dropped items.

5211.name: Player Skull
5211.desc: Gets a skull item representing a player. Skulls for other entities are provided by the aliases.

5216.name: Projectile Critical State
5216.desc: A projectile's critical state. The only currently accepted projectiles are arrows and tridents.

4990.name: Equip
4990.desc: Equips an entity with some given armor. This will replace any armor that the entity is wearing.

5026.name: Send Block Change
5026.desc: Makes a player see a block as something it really isn't. BlockData support is only for MC 1.13+

4779.name: On AoE Cloud Effect
4779.desc: Called when area effect cloud applies its potion effect. This happens every 5 ticks by default.

7618.name: AoE Cloud effect
7618.desc: Called when area effect cloud applies its potion effect. This happens every 5 ticks by default.

5077.name: Clicked Block/Entity/Inventory/Slot
5077.desc: The clicked block, entity, inventory, inventory slot, inventory click type or inventory action.
5077.changers:
add
set
remove
remove all
delete

4883.name: On Spread
4883.desc: Called when a new block forms as a result of a block that can spread, e.g. water or mushrooms.

4847.name: On Level Change
4847.desc: Called when a player's level changes, e.g. by gathering experience or by enchanting something.

4871.name: On Script Load/Unload
4871.desc: Called directly after the trigger is loaded, or directly before the whole script is unloaded.

10597.name: floor
10597.desc: Rounds a number down, i.e. returns the closest integer smaller than or equal to the argument.

4797.name: Click
4797.desc: Called when a user clicks on a block, an entity or air with or without an item in their hand.

5080.name: Command
5080.desc: The command that caused an 'on command' event (excluding the leading slash and all arguments)

5143.name: Highest Solid Block
5143.desc: Returns the highest solid block at the x and z coordinates of the world of a given location.
5143.changers:
add
set
remove
remove all
delete

5035.name: Teleport
5035.desc: Teleport an entity to a specific location.

5050.name: Alphabetical Sort
5050.desc: Sorts given strings in alphabetical order.

5068.name: Blocks in Region
5068.desc:
All blocks in a region.
This expression requires a supported regions plugin to be installed.
5068.changers:
add
set
remove
remove all
delete

5127.name: Food Level
5127.desc: The food level of a player from 0 to 10. Has several aliases: food/hunger level/meter/bar.

10573.name: Enchantment Type
10573.desc: An enchantment with an optional level, e.g. 'sharpness 2' or 'fortune'.

5153.name: Inventory Action
5153.desc: The inventory action of an inventory event. Please click on the link for more information.

5193.name: Minecart Derailed / Flying Velocity
5193.desc: The velocity of a minecart as soon as it has been derailed or as soon as it starts flying.

10596.name: While Loop
10596.desc: While Loop sections are loops that will just keep repeating as long as a condition is met.

4979.name: Charge Creeper
4979.desc: Charges or uncharges a creeper. A creeper is charged when it has been struck by lightning.

10620.name: ceil
10620.desc: Rounds a number up, i.e. returns the closest integer larger than or equal to the argument.

5114.name: Exhaustion
5114.desc: The exhaustion of a player. This is mainly used to determine the rate of hunger depletion.
5114.changers:
add
set
remove
remove all
delete
reset

5155.name: Inventory Slot
5155.desc: Represents a slot in an inventory. It can be used to change the item in an inventory too.
5155.changers:
add
set
remove
remove all
delete

5203.name: Offline players
5203.desc: All players that have ever joined the server. This includes the players currently online.

5089.name: Custom Model Data
5089.desc: Get/set the CustomModelData tag for an item. (Value is an integer between 0 and 99999999)
5089.changers:
add
set
remove
remove all
delete
reset

5121.name: Fall Distance
5121.desc: The distance an entity has fallen for.

5126.name: Flight Mode
5126.desc: Whether the player(s) are allowed to fly. Use Make Fly effect to force player(s) to fly.

10872.name: Is Climbing
10872.desc: Whether a living entity is climbing, such as a spider up a wall or a player on a ladder.

10624.name: vector
10624.desc: Creates a new vector, which can be used with various expressions, effects and functions.
10624.pattern: vector(x: number, y: number, z: number)

remove all

It has a <a href='#location'>location</a> and a <a href='#itemstack'>type</a>, and can also have a <a href='#direction'>direction</a> (mostly a <a href='expressions.html#ExprFacing'>facing</a>), an <a href='#inventory']world'>world</a>. An inventory has a fixed amount of [url='https://docs.skunity.com/syntax/types/slot'>slots</a> which represent a specific place in the inventory, e.g. the <a href='expressions.html#ExprArmorSlot']slot'>slots</a> which represent a specific place in the inventory, e.g. the <a href='expressions.html#ExprArmorSlot[/url] for players (Please note that slot support is still very limited but will be improved eventually).

10547.name: Player
10547.desc:
A player. Depending on whether a player is online or offline several actions can be performed with them, though you won't get any errors when using effects that only work if the player is online (e.g. changing their inventory) on an offline player.
You have two possibilities to use players as command arguments: <player> and <offline player>. The first requires that the player is online and also accepts only part of the name, while the latter doesn't require that the player is online, but the player's name has to be entered exactly.

Please note that while all effects and conditions that require a player can be used with an offline player as well, they will not work if the player is not actually online.

10561.name: Sound Category
10561.desc: The category of a sound, they are used for sound options of Minecraft. See the <a href='effects.html#EffPlaySound'>play sound</a> and <a href='effects.html#EffStopSound'>stop sound</a> effects.
10561.pattern: hostile creatures category, speech category, records category, friendly creature category, noteblock category, hostile creature category, note block category, voice category, ambient category, noteblocks category, note blocks category, weather category, block category, friendly mob category, jukebox category, hostile mob category, master category, master volume category, hostile category, record category, blocks category, environment category, jukeboxes category, player category, players category, hostile mobs category, friendly mobs category, music category, friendly creatures category, neutral category

10562.name: Gene
10562.desc: Represents a Panda's main or hidden gene. See <a href='https://minecraft.gamepedia.com/Panda#Genetics'>genetics</a> for more info.
10562.pattern: normal, lazy, happy, worried, worrisome, aggressive, brown, brownish, savage, playful, wild, weak

10567.name: Attribute Type
10567.desc: Represents the type of an attribute. Note that this type does not contain any numerical values.See <a href='https://minecraft.gamepedia.com/Attribute#Attributes'>attribute types</a> for more info.

10570.name: Region
10570.desc:
A region of a regions plugin. Skript currently supports WorldGuard, Factions, GriefPrevention and PreciousStones.
Please note that some regions plugins do not have named regions, some use numerical ids to identify regions, and some may have regions with the same name in different worlds, thus using regions like "region name" in scripts may or may not work.

10585.name: Damage Cause
10585.desc:
The cause/type of a <a href='events.html#damage'>damage event</a>, e.g. lava, fall, fire, drowning, explosion, poison, etc.
Please note that support for this type is very rudimentary, e.g. lava, fire and burning, as well as projectile and attack are considered different types.

10587.name: Object
10587.desc: The supertype of all types, meaning that if %object% is used in e.g. a condition it will accept all kinds of expressions.

7529.name: Colour Items
7529.desc: Colours items in a given <a href='classes.html#color'>colour</a>. You can also use RGB codes if you feel limited with the 16 default colours. RGB codes are three numbers from 0 to 255 in the order <code>(red, green, blue)</code>, where <code>(0,0,0)</code> is black and <code>(255,255,255)</code> is white. Armor is colourable for all Minecraft versions. With Minecraft 1.11 or newer you can also colour potions and maps. Note that the colours might not look exactly how you'd expect.

7531.name: Make Incendiary
7531.desc: Sets if an entity's explosion will leave behind fire. This effect is also usable in an explosion prime event.

7533.name: Open/Close Inventory
7533.desc: Opens an inventory to a player. The player can then access and modify the inventory as if it was a chest that he just opened.", "Please note that currently 'show' and 'open' have the same effect, but 'show' will eventually show an unmodifiable view of the inventory in the future.

7536.name: Break / Mine
7536.desc: Called when a block is broken by a player. If you use 'on mine', only events where the broken block dropped something will call the trigger.

7540.name: Form
7540.desc: Called when a block is created, but not by a player, e.g. snow forms due to snowfall, water freezes in cold biomes. This isn't called when block spreads (mushroom growth, water physics etc.), as it has its own event (see <a href='#spread'>spread event</a>).

7543.name: Chat
7543.desc: Called whenever a player chats. Use <a href='../expressions.html#ExprChatFormat'>chat format</a> to change message format, use <a href='../expressions.html#ExprChatRecipients'>chat recipients</a> to edit chat recipients.

7549.name: Item Spawn
7549.desc: Called whenever an item stack is spawned in a world, e.g. as drop of a block or mob, a player throwing items out of their inventory, or a dispenser dispensing an item (not shooting it).

7552.name: Pick Up
7552.desc: Called when a player picks up an item. Please note that the item is still on the ground when this event is called.

7553.name: Item Despawn
7553.desc: Called when an item is about to be despawned from the world, usually 5 minutes after it was dropped.

7554.name: Item Merge
7554.desc: Called when dropped items merge into a single stack. event-entity will be the entity which is trying to merge, and future event-entity will be the entity which is being merged into.

7555.name: Level Change
7555.desc: Called when a player's <a href='expressions.html#ExprLevel'>level</a> changes, e.g. by gathering experience or by enchanting something.

7560.name: Can Build Check
7560.desc: Called when a player rightclicks on a block while holding a block or a placeable item. You can either cancel the event to prevent the block from being built, or uncancel it to allow it.

7561.name: Block Damage
7561.desc: Called when a player starts to break a block. You can usually just use the leftclick event for this.

7562.name: Flow
7562.desc: Called when a blocks flows or teleports to another block. This not only applies to water and lava, but teleporting dragon eggs as well.

7563.name: Ignition
7563.desc: Called when a block starts burning, i.e. a fire block is placed next to it and this block is flammable.

7564.name: Physics
7564.desc: Called when a physics check is done on a block. By cancelling this event you can prevent some things from happening, e.g. sand falling, dirt turning into grass, torches dropping if their supporting block is destroyed, etc.Please note that using this event might cause quite some lag since it gets called extremely often.

7568.name: Spread
7568.desc: Called when a new block <a href='#form'>forms</a> as a result of a block that can spread, e.g. water or mushrooms.

7572.name: Creeper Power
7572.desc: Called when a creeper is struck by lighting and gets powered. Cancel the event to prevent the creeper from being powered.

7573.name: Zombie Break Door
7573.desc: Called when a zombie is done breaking a wooden door. Can be cancelled to prevent the zombie from breaking the door.

7574.name: Combust
7574.desc: Called when an entity is set on fire, e.g. by fire or lava, a fireball, or by standing in direct sunlight (zombies, skeletons).

7576.name: Portal Enter
7576.desc: Called when an entity enters a nether portal or an end portal. Please note that this event will be fired many times for a nether portal.

7578.name: Tame
7578.desc: Called when a player tames a wolf or ocelot. Can be cancelled to prevent the entity from being tamed.

7579.name: Explosion Prime
7579.desc: Called when an explosive is primed, i.e. an entity will explode shortly. Creepers can abort the explosion if the player gets too far away, while TNT will explode for sure after a short time.

7580.name: Hunger Meter Change
7580.desc: Called when the hunger bar of a player changes, i.e. either increases by eating or decreases over time.

7581.name: Fuel Burn
7581.desc: Called when a furnace burns an item from its <a href='expressions.html#ExprFurnaceSlot'>fuel slot</a>.

7582.name: Smelt
7582.desc: Called when a furnace smelts an item in its <a href='expressions.html#ExprFurnaceSlot'>ore slot</a>.

7585.name: Pig Zap
7585.desc: Called when a pig is stroke by lightning and transformed into a zombie pigman. Cancel the event to prevent the transformation.

7588.name: Bucket Empty
7588.desc: Called when a player empties a bucket. You can also use the <a href='#place'>place event</a> with a check for water or lava.

7590.name: Throwing of an Egg
7590.desc: Called when a player throws an egg. You can just use the <a href='#shoot'>shoot event</a> in most cases, as this event is intended to support changing the hatched mob and its chance to hatch, but Skript does not yet support that.

7593.name: Item Damage
7593.desc: Called when an item is damaged. Most tools are damaged by using them; armor is damaged when the wearer takes damage.

5290.name: Attribute Type
5290.desc: Represents the type of an attribute. Note that this type does not contain any numerical values.See attribute types for more info.

7594.name: Tool Change
7594.desc: Called whenever a player changes their held item by selecting a different slot (e.g. the keys 1-9 or the mouse wheel), <i>not</i> by dropping or replacing the item in the current slot.

7596.name: Entity Portal
7596.desc: Called when an entity uses a nether or end portal. <a href='effects.html#EffCancelEvent'>Cancel the event</a> to prevent the entity from teleporting.

7599.name: Sneak Toggle
7599.desc: Called when a player starts or stops sneaking. Use <a href='conditions.html#CondIsSneaking'>is sneaking</a> to get whether the player was sneaking before the event was called.

7600.name: Sprint Toggle
7600.desc: Called when a player starts or stops sprinting. Use <a href='conditions.html#CondIsSprinting'>is sprinting</a> to get whether the player was sprinting before the event was called.

5297.name: Click Type
5297.desc: Click type, mostly for inventory events. Tells exactly which keys/buttons player pressed, assuming that default keybindings are used in client side.

7601.name: Portal Create
7601.desc: Called when a portal is created, either by a player or mob lighting an obsidian frame on fire, or by a nether portal creating its teleportation target in the nether/overworld.

7607.name: Vehicle Damage
7607.desc: Called when a vehicle gets damage. Too much damage will <a href='#vehicle_destroy'>destroy</a> the vehicle.

7608.name: Vehicle Destroy
7608.desc: Called when a vehicle is destroyed. Any <a href='expressions.html#ExprPassenger'>passenger</a> will be ejected and the vehicle might drop some item(s).

7609.name: Vehicle Enter
7609.desc: Called when an <a href='classes.html#entity'>entity</a> enters a vehicle, either deliberately (players) or by falling into them (mobs).

7613.name: World Init
7613.desc: Called when a world is initialised. As all default worlds are initialised before any scripts are loaded, this event is only called for newly created worlds.

7614.name: World Load
7614.desc: Called when a world is loaded. As with the world init event, this event will not be called for the server's default world(s).

7615.name: World Save
7615.desc: Called when a world is saved to disk. Usually all worlds are saved simultaneously, but world management plugins could change this.

7616.name: World Unload
7616.desc: Called when a world is unloaded. This event might never be called if you don't have a world management plugin.

7617.name: Gliding State Change
7617.desc: Called when an entity toggles glider on or off, or when server toggles gliding state of an entity forcibly.

7623.name: Resurrect Attempt
7623.desc: Called when an entity dies, always. If they are not holding a totem, this is cancelled - you can, however, uncancel it.

7626.name: Language Change
7626.desc: Called after a player changed their language in the game settings. You can use the <a href='expressions.html#ExprLanguage'>language</a> expression to get the current language of the player.

7631.name: Riptide
7631.desc: Called when the player activates the riptide enchantment, using their trident to propel them through the air.

7642.name: Element of
7642.desc: The first, last or a random element of a set, e.g. a list variable.", "See also: <a href='#ExprRandom'>random</a>

7644.name: Firework Effect
7644.desc: Represents a 'firework effect' which can be used in the <a href='effects.html#EffFireworkLaunch'>launch firework</a> effect.
7644.pattern:
(1?|2?flickering|3?trailing|4?flickering trailing|5?trailing flickering) %fireworktype% [firework [effect]] colo[u]red %colors%
(1?|2?flickering|3?trailing|4?flickering trailing|5?trailing flickering) %fireworktype% [firework [effect]] colo[u]red %colors% fad(e|ing) [to] %colors%

7645.name: Hanging Entity/Remover
7645.desc: Returns the hanging entity or remover in hanging <a href='/events.html#break_mine'>break</a> and <a href='/events.html#place'>place</a> events.

7647.name: Inventory Holder/Viewers/Rows/Slots
7647.desc: Gets the amount of rows/slots, viewers and holder of an inventory.NOTE: 'Viewers' expression returns a list of players viewing the inventory. Note that a player is considered to be viewing their own inventory and internal crafting screen even when said inventory is not open.
7647.pattern:
(1?holder[s]|2?viewers|3?[amount of] rows|4?[amount of] slots) of %inventories%
%inventories%'[s] (1?holder[s]|2?viewers|3?[amount of] rows|4?[amount of] slots)

7648.name: Join & Split
7648.desc: Joins several texts with a common delimiter (e.g. ", "), or splits a text into multiple texts at a given delimiter.

split %string% (at|using|by) [[the] delimiter] %string%
%string% split (at|using|by) [[the] delimiter] %string%
regex split %string% (at|using|by) [[the] delimiter] %string%
regex %string% split (at|using|by) [[the] delimiter] %string%

7649.name: Plain Item
7649.desc: A plain item is an item with no modifications. It can be used to convert items to their default state or to match with other default items.

10977.name: Quit Reason
10977.desc: Represents a quit reason from a <a href='/events.html#quit'>player quit server event</a>.
10977.pattern: disconnected, erroneous state, kicked, quit, timed out, erroneous

7650.name: Potion Effect
7650.desc: Create a new potion effect to apply to an entity or item type. Do note that when applying potion effects ", "to tipped arrows/lingering potions, Minecraft reduces the timespan.

[new] ambient potion effect of %potioneffecttype% [potion] [[[of] tier] %-number%] [(1?without particles)] [for %-timespan%]

7651.name: Subtext
7651.desc: Extracts part of a text. You can either get the first <x> characters, the last <x> characters, the character at index <x>, or the characters between indices <x> and <y>. The indices <x> and <y> should be between 1 and the <a href='#ExprLength'>length</a> of the text (other values will be fit into this range).

7653.name: Whitelist
7653.desc: A server's whitelist.This expression can be used to add/remove players to/from the whitelist, to enable it and disable it (set whitelist to true / set whitelist to false), and to empty it (reset whitelist)

10614.name: calcExperience
10614.desc: Calculates the total amount of experience needed to achieve given level from scratch in Minecraft.

7634.name: Enchant Prepare
7634.desc: Called when a player puts an item into enchantment table. This event may be called multiple times.

7557.name: Pressure Plate / Trip
7557.desc: Called when a <i>player</i> steps on a pressure plate or tripwire respectively.

7567.name: Redstone
7567.desc: Called when the redstone current of a block changes. This event is of not much use yet.

7569.desc: Called when a chunk loads. The chunk might or might not contain mobs when it's loaded.

7604.name: Sign Change
7604.desc: As signs are placed empty, this event is called when a player is done editing a sign.

7592.name: Item Break
7592.desc: Called when a player breaks their tool because its damage reached the maximum value.

7606.name: Vehicle Create
7606.desc: Called when a new vehicle is created, e.g. when a player places a boat or minecart.

7636.name: Inventory Pickup
7636.desc: Called when an inventory (a hopper, a hopper minecart, etc.) picks up an item

7640.name: Item Mend
7640.desc: Called when a player has an item repaired via the Mending enchantment.

7548.name: Dispense

7625.name: Flight Toggle

13418.name: Advancement - Load
13418.desc:
Load an advancement represented by the specified string into the server.
The advancement format is governed by Minecraft and has no specified layout.
It is currently a JSON object, as described by [**McWiki**](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Advancement).
Loaded advancements will be stored and persisted across server restarts and reloads.
NOTE: Bukkit has marked this as 'Unsafe', so please use at your own risk.
Watch console for errors when loading an advancement.
