Useful, isn't it?This expression does not accept constructed queries because there is no need to use it. They can only be used with the find query.

13193.name: Skript - Effect Command String
13193.desc: The command used in an effect command event.\nThis doesn't include the prefix (usually `!`).\nCan be set, reset and deleted.
13193.pattern:
[the] [event-|the ][skript] effect command [string] of %[event-|the ][skript] effect command [string]%
%[event-|the ][skript] effect command [string]%'[s] [event-|the ][skript] effect command [string]

7050.name: User Locale
7050.desc:
Get the language code defined as user-side client of Discord.
Basically, return the language user's client is loaded in.
This expression only works in interactions event, and cannot be used outside of them.

7306.name: Mongo document JSON
7306.desc: Retrieve the JSON representation of the document. This expression can be useful to use it with skript-json and convert the document to a Skript variable, and vice versa. You can also define the JSON of the document.

2699.name: Sorted List By Values With Custom Format
2699.desc:
Returns sorted list with custom format of values.
Use @value and @index to manipulate content of variable list.
2699.pattern:
sorted %numbers% from highest to lowest with (output|format) %string%
sorted %numbers% from lowest to highest with (output|format) %string%

7307.name: Mongo document field
7307.desc: This expression is extremely important because it allows you to manage the values and lists of your documents. You can define lists, add items to lists, set values, or delete them. If Skript adapters are enabled, you can specify any type of data, and they will be automatically transformed by MongoSK so that they can be registered. So you can store players, blocks, items for example.

11915.name: Twitch Send Announce
11915.desc:
Send a announce to a channel!.
Colors: BLUE, GREEN, PURPLE, PRIMARY
If color is set to primary, the channel???s accent color is used to highlight the announcement

12427.name: Enchantment - Minimum Level
12427.desc:
Returns the Minimum Vanilla Level for an Enchantment.
There really isn't much of a reason to use this expression as every enchantment starts at 0.. 

Unless Mojang wants to prove me wrong.
12427.pattern:
[the] min[imum] enchant[ment] level of %enchantment%
%enchantment%'[s] min[imum] enchant[ment] level

7820.name: Iron Golem Disguise - Cracks
7820.desc:
Set or get the cracks in an iron golem disguise
The stages go from 1-4 (1 being no cracks and 4 being full of cracks)

12428.name: Ender Dragon Phase
12428.desc:
Returns the Ender Dragon phase in an Ender Dragon Phase Change Event.
Can be set. (Setting will always change the NEW phase)

7309.name: Mongo document values
7309.desc: With this expression, retrieve all the values of a document. The expression returns a list of different data types.

2702.name: On Chunk Enter/Leave
2702.desc:
Called when player moves between chunks (16x16 world areas).
Very good for protecting areas scripts like factions.

7310.name: Mongo filter
7310.desc: Create custom Mongo filters to target a certain type of data in your queries to your collections.The comparators are the same as for Skript.
7310.pattern:
[[a] new] mongo[(db|sk)] filter [where] field %string% is ((greater|more|higher|bigger|larger|above) [than] or (equal to|the same as)|\>=) %integer/number%
[[a] new] mongo[(db|sk)] filter [where] field %string% is (((greater|more|higher|bigger|larger) than|above)|\>) %integer/number%
[[a] new] mongo[(db|sk)] filter [where] field %string% is ((less|smaller|below) [than] or (equal to|the same as)|\<=) %integer/number%
[[a] new] mongo[(db|sk)] filter [where] field %string% is (((less|smaller) than|below)|\<) %integer/number%
[[a] new] mongo[(db|sk)] filter [where] field %string% is ((not|neither)|isn't|!=) [equal to] %integer/number/string/boolean/mongoskdocument%
[[a] new] mongo[(db|sk)] filter [where] field %string% (is|equals|=) %integer/number/string/boolean/mongoskdocument%
[[a] new] mongo[(db|sk)] filter [where] field %string% (does(n't| not) exist|is not (set|defined))
[[a] new] mongo[(db|sk)] filter [where] field %string% (exists|is (set|defined))

7311.name: Mongo find query
7311.desc: Use this expression if you want to make simple find requests, easily and quickly. To do so, you must specify the type of your query: are you looking for several documents or the first document in the collection? Then, the first means is to use a filter to specify the type of data you are looking for. Finally, you need to specify where the query should ask for the data, i.e. in which collection.The second way is to specify a Mongo request that you will have built beforehand. This will allow you to better specify your request and create a more complex one.You also have the possibility to modify already existing documents and delete documents, in the same way as for making your queries.
7311.pattern:
[find] (first|all) mongo[(sk|db)] document[s] [(with|by) [filter] %mongoskfilter%] (of|from) collection %mongoskcollection%
[find] (first|all) mongo[(sk|db)] document[s] (of|from) query %mongoskquery%

2704.name: Block Break Dropping Items
2704.desc:
Returns boolean if block in "on break" event is dropping items.
To set dropping in this event just set this expression to true or false.

7312.name: Mongo joined filters
7312.desc: Thanks to this expression, you will be able to combine two filters to refine your queries. Several types of filter comparison are possible, and, or, and nor.
7312.pattern:
mongo[(sk|db)] joined filters %mongoskfilter% (and|or|nor) %mongoskfilter%
mongo[(sk|db)] joined filters %mongoskfilters% with (and|or|nor) [join] mode

11920.name: Channel Image
11920.desc:
Returns the channel image of the channel.
This expression returns the channel image Url of the channel.
The Image is a 300x300 pixel image.

12432.name: Entity - Angry State
12432.desc:
Returns the Angry State of an entity.
(Warden, PigZombie, Wolf, Enderman)
Can be set for all except wardens.
12432.pattern:
[the] ang(ry|er) state of %entity%
%entity%'[s] ang(ry|er) state
whether %entity% is angry [or not]
whether [or not] %entity% is angry

11921.name: Chat Color
11921.desc: Returns the chat color of a userThis expression returns the chat color of a user in HEX format only if the user has set a chat color by himself.If the user has not set a chat color, this expression will return nothing.

13713.name: Simple json literal
13713.desc:
Explanatory notes
* - This expression is used to get a values (list) from a json object|array.
  - Need to be at the end of the path.


This syntax is a simplification for json path, and shortening the notation and getting closer to the form (jq or other popular tools)
**RECOMMENDATION**: Use this syntax exclusively for paths that are a maximum of 2 keys deep. - for Creating
- Use rather value/key path expression
Can handle strict (get/set/remove)
all variables or expressions must be in ?% ... %?
This syntax is strictly limited to its intended use; it does allow other expressions or variables to be used.
**RECOMMENDATION**: Use this syntax exclusively for paths that are a maximum of 2 keys deep.
Can handle strict (get/set/remove)
* at the end means you want to return a skript list.
13713.changers:
add
delete
remove
remove all
set

2706.name: Mox Data contains Mox Key
2706.desc:
Checks if Mox Data contains Mox Pair with given key.
Full tutorial: https://github.com/MorkaZ/MorkazSk/wiki/Mox-Data-tutorial
2706.pattern:
%moxdata% contain[s] [mox] pair with key[s] %strings%
%moxdata% do(esn't|es not| not) contain[s] [mox] pair with key[s] %strings%

3474.name: Knowledge Recipes
3474.desc: It returns a list of recipes of a knowledge book. You can either set, add and remove recipes, and clear/delete them all.

7058.name: Embed Color
7058.desc:
Get or change the color of an embed builder.
The color input must come from Skript, and will be converted by DiSky.
7058.changers:
add
set
remove
remove all
delete
reset

7314.name: Mongo name
7314.desc: Retrieve the names of different Mongo elements. You can use this expression to retrieve the name of collections or databases.

13714.name: Support literals
13714.desc: Returns the first, second, third, last, random or custom value of the json. This is used to get the first, second, third, last, random or custom value of the json.
13714.pattern:
[skjson] (1st|first) (value|key) of %jsonelement%
[skjson] (2nd|second) (value|key) of %jsonelement%
[skjson] (3rd|third) (value|key) of %jsonelement%
[skjson] last (value|key) of %jsonelement%
[skjson] random (value|key) of %jsonelement%
[skjson] %integer%. (value|key) of %jsonelement%

2707.name: Add Mox Pair to Mox Data
2707.desc:
This effect will add mox pair to chain of mox data.
Full tutorial: https://github.com/MorkaZ/MorkazSk/wiki/Mox-Data-tutorial

7059.name: Creation Date
7059.desc:
Get the creation date (as Skript date) of any ISnowFlake entity, including, but not limited to:
- Member
- User
- Role
- Guild
- Channel
- etc...

3476.name: Max Durability
3476.desc: Returns the max durability of {{types|ItemStack|item stack}}. i.e. 1561 for diamond sword. You can cancel it.

7316.name: Mongo query comment
7316.desc: Defines the comment of the request, in order to better monitor the query on your server. This is optional.

11924.name: Game Title
11924.desc: Returns the game title of the streamer. If the streamer is not currently streaming, it will NOT work

3477.name: Offline Player from UUID
3477.desc:
It get a player from a UUID. If you have Bensku's fork dev23+, you can just use {{expressions|Parse|parse expression}} using the uuid.
Also, the uuid needs to be from a player that already played on your server, else it will return null value.

7061.name: Name of Discord Entity
7061.desc:
This represent the current name of any discord entity that can hold one.
You can change name of every entity except member and user by defining a new text.
Check for 'nickname of member' if you want to check / change custom member's name.

7317.name: Mongo query disk usage
7317.desc: Enables writing to temporary files on the server. When set to true, the server can write temporary data to disk while executing the operation. This is optional.
7317.pattern:
[the] mongo[(db|sk)] disk usage of %mongoskqueries%
%mongoskqueries%'[s] mongo[(db|sk)] disk usage

12437.name: Entity - High Speed Swimming Splash Sound
12437.desc: Returns the Sound this entity makes when splashing in water at high speeds. For most entities, this is just 'ENTITY_GENERIC_SPLASH'.
12437.pattern:
[the] high speed swim[ming] splash sound of %entities%
%entities%'[s] high speed swim[ming] splash sound

3478.name: Online Time
3478.desc: Returns a {{types|Timespan|timespan}} of online time of {{types|Player|player}} or of the server. Only the online time of player can be edited.

7062.name: Emote Guild
7062.desc:
Get the guild that is attached to this emote.
Only emote have guild, emoji are from Discord and will therefore return none here.

7318.name: Mongo query filter
7318.desc: Allows you to set a filter associated with the query. This is optional for find queries, but mandatory for delete or replace queries!

2711.name: Keys of Mox Data
2711.desc:
Returns all Keys of Mox Data object.
Full tutorial: https://github.com/MorkaZ/MorkazSk/wiki/Mox-Data-tutorial

7063.name: Emote Name
7063.desc:
Get the name of this emote.
This, instead of 'discord name of %emote%' will return the name of an emote, and not an emoji.
You can change this property to change the emote's name itself.

11927.name: Twitch Channel Status
11927.desc: Returns the status of the Channel! If the channel is online, it will return 'ONLINE' else 'OFFLINE'. needs the channel name as input.

12439.name: Entity - Origin
12439.desc:
Gets the location where this entity originates from.
This value can be null if the entity hasn't yet been added to the world.

13719.name: attachment
13719.desc: Create new Attachment for the web request from path to file, when the file starts with */ the file will be found automatically.

2712.name: Mox Data
2712.desc:
Creates new instance of Mox Data.
You can create it empty or from text object.
Full tutorial: https://github.com/MorkaZ/MorkazSk/wiki/Mox-Data-tutorial
2712.pattern:
(new|empty) mox data
(new|empty) mox data with main key %string%
[new] mox data (of|from) %string%
[new] mox data (of|from) %string% with main key %string%

3480.name: RGB Color
3480.desc:
Returns the rgb color of {{types|ItemStack|item stack}} or {{types|Color|color}}. You can set these values only for item stacks, in this case, leather armors.
The RGB color returns a list with 3 numbers and the other expressions returns which one separated.
3480.version: 1.5.3 (single value of items), 1.6 (list values of items and color)

7064.name: Emote Image URL
7064.desc:
Get the URL of this emote.
Only emote have image URL, emoji are from Discord and will therefore return none here.

12440.name: Entity - Pose
12440.desc: Returns the entity's current pose. Note that the pose is only updated at the end of a tick, so it may be inconsistent.

3481.name: Rabbit Type
3481.desc: Returns the type of rabbit. e.g. `black`, `black and white`, `brown`, `gold`, `salt and pepper`, `the killer bunny` and `white`.

7065.name: Guild Of
7065.desc:
Return the guild of a specific entity.
This can return null if the entity is not guild-based, like private message channel or message.

3482.name: Recipe ID
3482.desc: Starting from minecraft 1.12, the recipes now has a unique id. Recipes registered by minecraft will have a id `minecraft:%the result item's name%`, an old recipe plugin will be `bukkit:%random uuid%`, while TuSKe will have its id as `tuske:%last recipe id + 1%`. Other plugins may have a different format, but always following `<plugin>:<key>`.**Only for Shaped and Shapeless recipes**

7322.name: Mongo server
7322.desc: Create a connection to your remote MongoDB host using this expression.This syntax requires to specify a valid MongoDB connection string.Don't forget to include the 'appName' option in order to improve MongoSK reports in case of problems and to identify requests to your server monitoring.You can consult the attached examples or the official documentation: https://docs.mongodb.com/manual/reference/connection-string/.

3483.name: Recipe Owner
3483.desc: Starting from minecraft 1.12, recipes have now the register plugin. If it is a minecraft recipe, it will return as `Minecraft`, if it is an old recipe plugin, it will return as `Bukkit` and everything else will return the plugin's name. **Only for Shaped and Shapeless recipes**

7067.name: Guild Booster Role
7067.desc:
Represent the booster role of this guild.
Any member that got this role is actually a booster of the guild.

2716.name: Values of Mox Data
2716.desc:
Returns all Values of Mox Data object.
Full tutorial: https://github.com/MorkaZ/MorkazSk/wiki/Mox-Data-tutorial

3484.name: Regex Error
3484.desc: It contains the last error of a regex. It is setted when there is a error while parsing a string as regex, {{effects|RegexReplace|replacing}}/{{effects|RegexSplit|spliting}} a string or checking in the {{conditions|RegexMatches|condition}}

7068.name: Everyone Role
7068.desc:
Represent the @everyone role of a guild.
Even if it's not a real role, it share multiple properties such as permissions.

2717.name: Mox Data Type
2717.desc:
Mox Data type. It can hold multiple values indexed by keys in one field called Mox Chain.
Specially created for databases to not create a lot of columns but it can be also used in normal skript features - for example in NBT Tags.

7069.name: Guild Verification Level
7069.desc:
Represent the verification level of the guild. It can either be:
- None
- Low
- Medium
- High
- Very High

7325.name: New Mongo query
7325.desc: This expression will allow you to create a new Mongo query, which you can refine with the many expressions available.

2718.name: Mox Pair Type
2718.desc:
Mox Pair type. It holds key and value. Useable in Mox Data operations
Specially created for databases to not create a lot of columns but can be also used in common scripting.

3486.name: Split Characters
3486.desc: Split a text with {{types|Number|number}} amount of characters. It is used to split the message in chat (the default is 60) and to item's lore.

3487.name: Custom Enchantment
3487.desc: It represents a custom enchantment. The values depends of the id name of {{effects|RegisterEnchantment|registered enchantment}}.

12447.name: Entity - Swimming Splash Sound
12447.desc: Returns the Sound this entity makes when splashing in water. For most entities, this is just 'ENTITY_GENERIC_SPLASH'.
12447.pattern:
[the] swim[ming] splash sound of %entity%
%entity%'[s] swim[ming] splash sound

3488.name: GUI
3488.desc: It represents a gui inventory, where the player can take items away from the inventory. It can be created only with {{effects|MakeGUI|advanced gui effect}}.

12448.name: Entity - Variant
12448.desc:
Returns the Variant of an Entity.
Parrot: blue, cyan, green, red
Frog: cold, temperate, warm
Mushroom Cow: red, brown
Axolotl: blue, cyan, gold, lucy, wild
Llama: brown, creamy, gray, white
Fox: red, snow
Cat: all_black, black, british_shorthair, calico, jellie, persian, ragdoll, red, siamese, tabby, white
Rabbit: black, black_and_white, brown, gold, salt_and_pepper, the_killer_bunny, white
Panda: aggressive, brown, lazy, normal, playful, weak, worried
Tropical Fish: betty, blockfish, brinely, clayfish, dasher, flopper, glitter, kob, snooper, spotty, stripey, sunstreak

3489.name: Recipe
3489.desc: A recipe contains the the ingredients list and the result item. Can only be get by {{expressions|Recipes|recipes's expression}}.

3490.name: Regex
3490.desc: Represents an regex pattern object, it can be created with `"regex here" parsed as regex` or `/regex here/`. The second option is useful cause you don't need to escape Skript characters (like double %%, ""). Obviously, you can't use Skript expression in it, so for thatyou will need the first option.

7076.name: Member Effective Name
7076.desc:
Simple way to get the effective name of a member in a guild:
If the nickname is not set, it will return the discord name of the member, else its nickname.

7077.name: Member Join Date
7077.desc:
Represent the skript's date of the member's join date.
It cannot be changed.
This is a specific element of the bot, so it can be used in the bots event.

12453.name: Fox - Properties
12453.desc:
Various fox properties.
Everything in this expression can be used with `Paper`.
With `Spigot` you can only:
 - `Get` and `Set` the Crouching State and Sleeping State
 - `Get` the Faceplanted State
12453.pattern:
[the] fox [is] (leaping|crouching|defending|sleeping|face[ ]planted) state of %livingentity%
%livingentity%'[s] fox [is] (leaping|crouching|defending|sleeping|face[ ]planted) state
whether [the] fox %livingentity% is (leaping|crouching|defending|sleeping|face[ ]planted) [or not]
whether [or not] [the] fox %livingentity% is (leaping|crouching|defending|sleeping|face[ ]planted)

7078.name: Member Nickname
7078.desc:
Represent the member nickname. Can be none if the member doesn't have any nickname currently.
USe 'effective name' expression to get member's name of its nickname is not set.

11942.name: User Image
11942.desc:
Returns the user image of the user.
This expression returns the user image Url of the user.
The Image is a 300x300 pixel image.

12454.name: Fox - Trusted Players
12454.desc:
Returns the first, second, or both trusted players of 1 or more foxes.
First and second can both be set to a single offline player, trusted players can be set to 2 offline players (or 1, which only sets the first one).

Note: Before the second trusted player of a fox can be set, the first one must also be set, in the same way, you can't clear the first one if the second one is set, trying to do either of those things won't do anything

If you wish to set/clear both, do so by using the second pattern: `clear trusted players of {_fox}`
12454.pattern:
[the] [first|second] trusted player of %livingentities%
%livingentities%'[s] [first|second] trusted player
[the] trusted players of %livingentities%
%livingentities%'[s] trusted players

7079.name: Member Status
7079.desc:
Represent the member's online status.
The online status is represented by the following values:
- `online`
- `offline`
- `idle`
- `do not disturb`
- `invisible`

7080.name: Mention Tag
7080.desc:
Get the mention name of the discord entity.
It will return the similar format that when you are doing @ (roles, users) or # (channels) followed by names.

7081.name: Message User Author
7081.desc: Get the user instance of the message's author. Can be null in case of the message was sent by a webhook.

11946.name: On Subscription Event
11946.desc:
Triggered when a user subscribe in the given stream.
Please note that the Channels have to mention in the Login Code

11947.name: On Stop Live
11947.desc:
Called when a given Twitch channel goes Offline
Please note that the Channels have to mention in the Login Code

11948.name: On Live Chat Message
11948.desc:
Triggered when a message is written in the given stream.
Please note that the Channels have to mention in the Login Code

173.name: Client Chest
173.pattern:
[skellett] (1?open|2?close) [the] %block% for %players%
[skellett] make [the] %block% (appear|look) (1?open|2?closed) for %players%
[skellett] play chest (1?open|2?close) animation at %block% for %players%

11949.name: On Going Live
11949.desc:
Called when a given Twitch channel goes Live
Please note that the Channels have to mention in the Login Code

12973.name: Blueprint - Save/Load/Delete Blueprint
12973.desc:
Saves/Loads/Deletes a blueprint from `plugins/Skuishy/blueprints/`.
### SAVE NOTE: if the blueprint already exists, it will overwrite.
12973.pattern:
save %blueprint% (as|with name) %string%
load [saved] blueprint (with name|named) %string% and (store|put) it in %object%
delete [saved] blueprint (with name|named) %string%

13741.name: Translate Specific
13741.desc:
Different from the Translate effect in that it specifies the current language of the string
This can help to reduce misunderstandings caused by the auto-detect language.
13741.pattern:
translate %strings% to %language% from %language%
translate %strings% from %language% to %language%

11950.name: On Gift Subscription Event
11950.desc:
Triggered when a user subscribe in the given stream.
Please note that the Channels have to mention in the Login Code

13742.name: Language From Code
13742.desc: Returns the language from a language code. Language codes can be viewed here: https://cloud.google.com/translate/docs/languages

7087.name: Profile Banner
7087.desc:
Get the profile banner URL. If the user doesn't have a custom banner, this will return none.
Use the 'profile color' expression to get the color instead of the banner URL in that case!

11951.name: On Follow Event
11951.desc:
Triggered when a user follow in the given stream.
Please note that the Channels have to mention in the Login Code

12463.name: Item - Rarity
12463.desc:
Returns the rarity of an item.
Can be set.

Before Lusk 1.2 (and Minecraft 1.20.5), this expression returned strings and also worked for enchantments, due to some major changes enchantments no longer have a rarity.

7088.name: Profile Color
7088.desc:
Get the profile color accent. If the user have a custom banner, this will return none.
Use the 'profile banner' expression to get the avatar URL instead of the color accent in that case!

11952.name: On Cheer Event
11952.desc:
Triggered when a user cheer in the given stream.
Please note that the Channels have to mention in the Login Code

3249.name: Vehicle  Steer
3249.desc: Called on every vehicle move packet. Strings are WASD,SHIFT and SPACEBAR. If no key is pressed,the event-string will be "NONE"

7089.name: User Discriminator
7089.desc:
Represent the four digit number after the # of a user's name.
These, mixed with the user name itself, are unique.
This **DOES NOT** include the `#` char, so you have to add it yourself.

11953.name: On Game Change Event
11953.desc:
Triggered when a game changed in the given stream.
Please note that the Channels have to mention in the Login Code
11953.pattern:
twitch game change [event]
	send event-gametitle to console

12465.name: Item Frame - Rotation
12465.desc:
Returns the rotation of an Item Frame in Degrees.
Can be set to the following values:
0, 45, 90, 135, 180, 225, 270, 315

7090.name: Continue State of Guild
7090.desc:
Get ot set the continue state of a guild.
If it's true, and there's a next track available once the current finish, it will play it..

11954.name: On Raid Event
11954.desc:
Triggered when a user raid in the given stream.
Please note that the Channels have to mention in the Login Code

12466.name: Item Rarity - Color
12466.desc:
Returns the color of an item's rarity.
Can be used with the item itself and it will get its rarity's color without getting the rarity itself if you don't need it.

11955.name: On Custom Reward Event
11955.desc:
Triggered when a user redeem a custom reward in the given stream.
Please note that the Channels have to mention in the Login Code

11957.name: On Clip Create Event
11957.desc:
Triggered when a clip is created in the given stream.
Please note that the Channels have to mention in the Login Code

13749.name: Armadillo - roll Out/Up
13749.desc: Attempts to roll the provided armadillos up (if they're idle) or out (if they're not idle).

7095.name: Track Position
7095.desc:
Return the position of a specific track
This property can eb changed to move the current position of the track.
It will only accept timespan (e.g. '1 second', '25 minutes', etc...)!

13752.name: Armor Stand - is Small (Property)
13752.desc: Gets and sets the `small` property of an armorstand entity or item, to do so with an armorstand item you must have Paper.

13753.name: Block/BlockData/BlockState/Item - Slipperiness
13753.desc:
Returns a value that represents how 'slippery' the block is.
Blocks with higher slipperiness, like ice can be slid on further by the player and other entities.
Most blocks have a default slipperiness of 0.6.

Can be used with items, blocks, blockstates, and blockdatas.

7354.name: On Discord Command
7354.desc: Custom DiSky discord command system. Arguments works like the normal skript's one and accept both optional and require arguments.
7354.eventvalues:
event-guildchannel
event-discordcommand
event-channel
event-string
event-guild
event-member
event-user
event-message
event-bot

7356.name: On Dropdown Click
7356.desc:
Fired when an user select one or more choice in a dropdown.
Use 'event-dropdown' to get the dropdown id. Don't forget to either reply or defer the interaction.
Modal can be shown in this interaction.
7356.eventvalues:
event-privatechannel
event-newschannel
event-threadchannel
event-guild
event-message
event-guildchannel
event-channel
event-textchannel
event-string
event-dropdown
event-member
event-user
event-bot

7358.name: On Guild Owner Event
7358.desc: Fired when a owner of a guild changes can be used to get the old/new owner, the author and the guild.
7358.eventvalues:
past event-member
event-guild
event-member
event-bot
future event-member

7359.name: On Guild Icon Event
7359.desc: Fired when the icon of a guild changes can be used to get the old/new icon, the author and the guild.
7359.eventvalues:
past event-string
event-string
event-guild
event-bot
future event-string

13759.name: Entity - Should Burn During The Day (Property)
13759.desc:
Returns whether or not the provided entities should burn during the day.
Applies to zombies, skeletons (all types), and phantoms

In 1.17.1 this doesn't work with skeleton variants, such as strays, but it does work with base skeletons.

Can be set.

12480.name: Small Capital Case
12480.desc:
Returns the given string with the small font.
'Strict' allows uppercase characters to be included.

13760.name: Entity - is Angry (Property)
13760.desc:
Returns the Angry Property of an entity. (Warden, PigZombie, Wolf, Enderman)
Can be set for all except wardens.

To use this for endermen `Paper 1.18.2+` is required.

11969.name: Is Action
11969.desc: This condition checks if the player has interacted with a custom block with either a left or a right click.

12481.name: Trident - Loyalty
12481.desc:
Returns loyalty level of a thrown trident.

Allows: Setting, Removing, Adding, Deleting and Resetting.

This value will always be between 0 and 127.

Changing this value won't influence the item itself, just the throw trident.

13761.name: Entity - is Interested (Property)
13761.desc:
Returns whether or not the provided foxes or wolves are interested.
Paper 1.18.2+ is required to use this with foxes.

12482.name: Used Tool/Used Hand/Used Equipment Slot
12482.desc:
Retrieves the used hand or item used in events where either hand is used.
The first pattern returns the Slot (Item + Index) of the item in the used hand.
- Note: using this is not the same as using `event-slot` or `event-item`, if either is available, use that
The second pattern returns an Equipment Slot that's either `hand_slot` or `off_hand_slot`.

Supported Events:
- on Right Click
- on Item Consume
- on Arm Swing
- on Entity Shoot (different than 'on Shoot'!)
- on Crossbow Load
- on Place (includes 'on Block Place', 'on Hanging Place', and 'on Entity Place')
- on Resurrect
- on Player Fish
- on Bucket Fill
- on Bucket Empty
- on Elytra Boost
- on Player Harvest
- on Can Build Check
- on Player Shear Entity
- on Player Leash Entity
- on Player Unleash Entity
- on Player Use Unknown Entity
12482.changers:
add
set
remove
remove all
delete

13762.name: Entity - is Sitting (Property)
13762.desc:
Returns whether an entity is sat. Can be set.
This works for Cats, Wolves, Parrots, Pandas and Foxes.
On Paper 1.20.1+ it applies for some other entities which have a SITTING pose.

7363.name: On Guild Splash Event
7363.desc: Fired when a banner of a guild changes can be used to get the old/new banner, the author and the guild.
7363.eventvalues:
past event-string
event-string
event-guild
event-bot
future event-string

13763.name: Player - Player Tab List Order
13763.desc:
Returns the relative order that the player is shown on the player list.
Can be set, added to and removed from.

Setting this modifies the order for the player you're setting it for.

7364.name: On Invite Create Event
7364.desc: Fired when a invite is created in a guild can be used to get the invite property, the author and the guild.

12484.name: Vindicator - Johnny State
12484.desc:
Get and Set whether 1 or more vindicators are Johnny.
Changing this does not modify the vindicator's name.
12484.pattern:
[the] [vindicator] is johnny state of %livingentities%
%livingentities%'[s] [vindicator] is johnny state
whether [the] [vindicator[s]] %livingentities% (is|are) johnny [or not]
whether [or not] [the] [vindicator[s]] %livingentities% (is|are) johnny

13764.name: Sign - is Editable (Property)
13764.desc:
Returns whether or not the provided signs are editable.
Can be set and reset (which makes it editable).

7365.name: On Invite Delete Event
7365.desc: Fired when a invite is deleted from a guild can be used to get the invite property, the author and the guild.

7366.name: On Member Accept Screen Event
7366.desc: Fired when a member has agreed to membership screen requirements it can be useful for adding roles since the member is not available if they haven't accepted it yet.
7366.eventvalues:
past event-boolean
event-guild
event-member
event-boolean
event-bot
future event-boolean

12486.name: Warden - Anger
12486.desc:
Returns the anger of a warden.

Angry = 80-150
Agitated = 40-79
Calm = 0-39

Use the respective conditions to check for those 3 states.

7368.name: On Member Leave Event
7368.desc: Fired when a member is removed from a guild either by leaving or being punished. Use the ban/kick event instead to check the exact reason

7369.name: On Message Command
7369.desc:
Fired when someone click on a message application command.
Use 'event-string' to get the command name. Don't forget to either reply to the interaction. Defer doesn't work here.
Modal can be shown in this interaction.
7369.eventvalues:
event-guildchannel
event-channel
event-privatechannel
event-textchannel
event-string
event-newschannel
event-threadchannel
event-guild
event-member
event-user
event-message
event-bot

2762.name: Get Mox Pair of Mox Data by Key
2762.desc:
Returns Mox Pair from Mox Data by given key. If pair will not be found, it will be <none>.
Full tutorial: https://github.com/MorkaZ/MorkazSk/wiki/Mox-Data-tutorial
2762.pattern:
[mox] pair of %moxdata% (by [key]|that contain[s] [key]|with key|key[[ed] by]) %string%
[mox] pair (with key|key[[ed] by]|that contain[s] key) %string% (of|from) %moxdata%

7370.name: On Message Delete
7370.desc:
Fired when any message is deleted.
Use 'event-string' to get the old message content, only works if this message was cached by DiSky before hand.
This will be fired, by default, both guild & private messages, use the 'event is from guild' condition to avoid confusion.
7370.eventvalues:
event-guildchannel
event-channel
event-privatechannel
event-textchannel
event-string
event-newschannel
event-threadchannel
event-guild
event-bot

2763.name: Key Name of Mox Pair
2763.desc:
Returns Key Name of Mox Pair.
Full tutorial: https://github.com/MorkaZ/MorkazSk/wiki/Mox-Data-tutorial

7371.name: On Message Edit
7371.desc:
Fired when any message is edited / updated.
Use 'event-string' to get the old message content, only works if this message was cached by DiSky before hand.
This will be fired, by default, both guild & private messages, use the 'event is from guild' condition to avoid confusion.
7371.eventvalues:
event-guildchannel
event-channel
event-privatechannel
event-textchannel
event-string
event-newschannel
event-threadchannel
event-guild
event-message
event-bot

2764.name: Main Key of Mox Data
2764.desc:
Returns main key of Mox Data. Usually it is index name, for example: player name, uuid.
Full tutorial: https://github.com/MorkaZ/MorkazSk/wiki/Mox-Data-tutorial

7372.name: On Message Receive
7372.desc:
Fired when any bot receive an actual message.
This will be fired, by default, both guild & private messages, use the 'event is from guild' condition to avoid confusion.
7372.eventvalues:
event-guildchannel
event-channel
event-privatechannel
event-textchannel
event-newschannel
event-threadchannel
event-guild
event-member
event-user
event-message
event-bot

2765.name: Mox Pairs of Mox Data
2765.desc:
Returns all Mox Pairs of Mox Data object.
Full tutorial: https://github.com/MorkaZ/MorkazSk/wiki/Mox-Data-tutorial

7373.name: On Modal Receive
7373.desc:
Fired when a modal has been sent to the bot from any user.
Use 'event-string' to get the modal id. Don't forget to either reply or defer the interaction.
Modal can NOT be shown in this interaction.
7373.eventvalues:
event-guildchannel
event-channel
event-privatechannel
event-textchannel
event-string
event-newschannel
event-threadchannel
event-guild
event-member
event-user
event-bot

7374.name: On Reaction Add
7374.desc:
Fired when a message, that can be seen by the bot, receive a reaction.
This will be fired, by default, both guild & private messages, use the 'event is from guild' condition to avoid confusion.
7374.eventvalues:
event-guildchannel
event-channel
event-privatechannel
event-textchannel
event-emote
event-newschannel
event-threadchannel
event-guild
event-member
event-user
event-bot

7375.name: On Reaction Remove
7375.desc:
Fired when an user remove a reaction from a specific message.
This will be fired, by default, both guild & private messages, use the 'event is from guild' condition to avoid confusion.
7375.eventvalues:
event-guildchannel
event-channel
event-privatechannel
event-textchannel
event-emote
event-newschannel
event-threadchannel
event-guild
event-member
event-user
event-bot

7888.name: Broadcast message to the network
7888.desc: Broadcast message to the network, like the /alert command does but with more personalization (the messages will not appear in the spigot consoles)

13008.name: On Block - on Ignite [Lusk Extension]
13008.desc:
**THIS IS AN EXTENDED VERSION OF SKRIPT'S IGNITE EVENT.**

`event-player` = the Player that placed/ignited the fire block, or not set if not ignited by a Player.

`event-entity` = the Entity that placed/ignited the fire block, or not set if not ignited by an Entity.

`event-ignitecause` = the value detailing the cause of the block ignition.

Called when a block is ignited. If you want to catch when a Player places fire, use the place event.
If this event is cancelled, the block will not be ignited.
13008.eventvalues:
event-block
event-entity
event-ignitecause
event-location
event-player
event-world

7377.name: On Role Add Event
7377.desc: Fired when a member adds roles to another member, it's a log action so event-author returns who made the action event-roles returns a list of added roles

13009.name: On Player - on Interact
13009.desc:
Called when a player interacts with a block or entity by clicking.

This event is always called unlike Skript's click event, meaning that it can be called for both hands.

You can use `main hand` and `off hand` to make it per hand.

`event-equipmentslot` = the slot of the used hand
`event-blockaction` = the action of this event
`event-vector` = the vector from the player to the interaction point
`event-location` = the location of the interaction point
13009.eventvalues:
event-block
event-blockaction
event-direction
event-entity
event-equipmentslot
event-itemstack
event-location
event-player
event-vector
event-world

13010.name: Anvil GUI - Can Be Closed
13010.desc:
Checks if an anvil gui can be closed.
This is only true if the `Anvil GUI - Prevent Closing` effect is used and cannot be reversed without creating a new gui.

7380.name: On Role Remove Event
7380.desc: Fired when a member removes roles from another member, it's a log action so event-author returns who made the action event-roles returns a list of removed roles

7381.name: On Slash Command
7381.desc:
Fired when a user execute a specific slash command.
Use 'event-string' to get the command name. Don't forget to either reply or defer the interaction, You can only defer using the wait pattern  e.g: 'defer the interaction and wait [silently].
Modal can be shown in this interaction.
You can get value of arguments using 'argument "name" as string' for example.
7381.eventvalues:
event-guildchannel
event-channel
event-privatechannel
event-textchannel
event-string
event-newschannel
event-threadchannel
event-guild
event-member
event-user
event-bot

7382.name: On Slash Completion
7382.desc:
Fired when Discord ask an argument completion.
Use 'event-string' to get the command name. Use normal return effect to return the actual completions.
Modal can NOT be shown in this interaction.
7382.eventvalues:
event-guildchannel
event-channel
event-privatechannel
event-textchannel
event-string
event-newschannel
event-threadchannel
event-guild
event-member
event-user
event-bot

12502.name: Click Section
12502.desc:
Runs the code inside of it when the provided entity gets clicked.
Local Variables that are:
- defined BEFORE this section CAN be used inside of it.
- defined AFTER this section CANNOT be used inside of it.
- defined INSIDE this section CANNOT be used outside of it.

7383.name: On Thread Join Event
7383.desc: Fired when a member joins a tread, either by joining itself or by a moderator can be used to get the thread, the guild and the member.

12503.name: Damage Section
12503.desc:
"Runs the code inside of it when the provided entity takes damage.
Local Variables that are:
- defined BEFORE this section CAN be used inside of it.
- defined AFTER this section CANNOT be used inside of it.
- defined INSIDE this section CANNOT be used outside of it.
12503.pattern:
[execute|run] on damage of %entity%
[execute|run] when %entity% get[s] damaged

7384.name: On Thread Leave Event
7384.desc: Fired when a member leaves a thread, either by leaving itself or by a moderator can be used to get the thread, the guild and the member.

10712.name: User/Player Name
10712.desc:
Usable only in CoreProtect logging event.
The name of the user under which this action will be logged.
This value can be changed.
This can be referred as 'event-string', which only the getter is provided.

13016.name: Block - is Full Block
13016.desc:
Checks if a block is a full block (like dirt, stone, endstone).
Essentially checks if a block is 1x1x1 and only has one mesh.
13016.pattern:
%blocks/blockstates% (is|are) [a] full block[s]
%blocks/blockstates% (isn't|is not|aren't|are not) [a] full block[s]

12505.name: Heal Section
12505.desc:
Runs the code inside of it when the provided entity gets healed.
Local Variables that are:
- defined BEFORE this section CAN be used inside of it.
- defined AFTER this section CANNOT be used inside of it.
- defined INSIDE this section CANNOT be used outside of it.
12505.pattern:
[execute|run] on heal of %entity%
[execute|run] when %entity% get[s] healed

2522.name: Delete World
2522.desc: Deletes the specified world. The specified world must be loaded in order to be deleted. There should also not be any players in the specified world when it is deleted.

7386.name: On User Command
7386.desc:
Fired when someone click on an user application command.
Use 'event-string' to get the command name. Don't forget to either reply to the interaction. Defer doesn't work here.
Modal can be shown in this interaction.
7386.eventvalues:
event-guildchannel
event-channel
event-privatechannel
event-textchannel
event-string
event-newschannel
event-threadchannel
event-guild
event-member
event-user
event-bot

13018.name: BlockState - is Placed
13018.desc:
Checks whether the provided blockstates are placed in a world, if not, they are 'virtual' (e. g. on an item).
Some syntaxes will not work if the block state isn't placed in the world.

2523.name: Duplicate World
2523.desc: Creates a copy of the specified world using the specified string as a name. The specified world must be loaded in order for this to work.

10715.name: Lookup
10715.desc:
Performs a lookup.
This effect causes a delay of the script execution.
Objects specified with 'on' and 'expect on' can be Entity Data, Entity Types, Item Types or Block Data.
Use 'results' in this section to get the results of the lookup.
10715.pattern: lookup [action] (data|logs) in [last] %timespan% [for %strings%] [except for %strings%] [on %objects%] [except on %objects%] [with ([an] action|actions) %integers%] [in radius %integer%] [at %location%]

13019.name: Bounding Box - Overlaps
13019.desc:
Whether or not one or more bounding boxes overlap other bounding boxes.
Bounding boxes that are only intersecting at the borders are not considered overlapping.

2524.name: Load World Automatically
2524.desc: Tells Kosmos whether it should load the specified world automatically on server start. This is useful for simple and straightforward world management without the need for a world management plugin. Don't run this effect with the main world, as Bukkit will already load that world automatically, and this effect can't be used to enable/disable that behavior.

10461.name: Async Request
10461.desc:
Executes request to url
(cannot return values if used in functions, but not affect server performance)
10461.pattern: [async[hronously]] request [%-string%] to [url] %string% [with header[s] %-requestproperties%] [(and|with) body %-string%] [and store [[the] (body|result) in %-object%] [and] [code in %-object%]]

13021.name: Crossbow - has Charged Projectiles
13021.desc:
Checks if one or more crossbows have any charged projectiles at all.
This behaves the same way the `is charged` condition behaves for crossbows.
13021.pattern:
%itemtypes% (has|have) charged projectiles
%itemtypes% (doesn't|does not|do not|don't) have charged projectiles

10462.name: sync Request
10462.desc:
Executes request to url
(cannot return values if used in functions, but not affect server performance)
10462.pattern: sync[hronously] request [%-string%] to [url] %string% [with header[s] %-requestproperties%] [(and|with) body %-string%] [and store [[the] (body|result) in %-object%] [and] [code in %-object%]]

11998.name: Create Custom Inventory
11998.desc:
Creates a new ItemsAdder inventory with the following properties:
- Title: The title of the inventory. This will be displayed at the top of the inventory GUI.
- Rows: The number of rows in the inventory. Each row corresponds to 9 slots, so an inventory with 3 rows would have 26 slots. You start at slot 0, so thats why its 26, not 27.)
- Texture: The texture of the inventory. This should be the name of a texture defined in your ItemsAdder configuration. You may also have multple strings/textures here.
- Title Offset: The horizontal offset of the title in pixels. This can be used to adjust the position of the title relative to the top of the inventory GUI.
- Texture Offset: The horizontal offset of the texture in pixels. This can be used to adjust the position of the texture relative to the top of the inventory GUI.
The last created inventory can be accessed using the 'Last Created Gui' expression.
To create an Inventory, you need a Texture, everything else is optional. See Examples for a demonstration.

12767.name: On Block - Dispense Armor
12767.desc:
Called when an equippable item is dispensed from a block and equipped on a nearby entity.
If a Block Dispense Armor event is cancelled, the equipment will not be equipped on the target entity.
12767.eventvalues:
event-block
event-entity
event-itemstack
event-location
event-vector
event-world

13024.name: Ender Signal - is Going to Drop/Shatter
13024.desc: Checks if the provided ender signals should drop an item on death. If true, they will drop an item. If false, they will shatter.
13024.pattern:
[ender (signal|eye)] %entities% (is|are) going to (drop|shatter)
[ender (signal|eye)] %entities% (isn't|is not|aren't|are not) going to (drop|shatter)

12769.name: On Block - Entity Block Form
12769.desc:
Called when a block is formed by entities.
Examples:
- Snow formed by a org. bukkit. entity. Snowman.
- Frosted Ice formed by the Frost Walker enchantment.
12769.eventvalues:
event-block
event-entity
event-location
event-world
past event-block

13025.name: Entity - is Aggressive
13025.desc:
Checks if the provided entities are aggressive.

Some mobs will raise their arm(s) when aggressive:
Drowned, Piglin, Skeleton, Zombie, ZombieVillager, Illusioner, Vindicator, Panda, Pillager, PiglinBrute

Note: This doesn't always return the actual aggressive state as when set, Pandas are always aggressive if their combined Panda Gene is AGGRESSIVE.

12771.name: On Block - Mutli Place
12771.desc: Fired when a single block placement action of a player triggers the creation of multiple blocks(e. g. placing a bed block).
12771.eventvalues:
event-block
event-boolean
event-direction
event-itemstack
event-location
event-player
event-world
future event-itemstack
past event-block
past event-itemstack

13028.name: Item Frame - is Fixed
13028.desc:
Returns whether the item frame is "fixed" or not.
When true it's not possible to destroy/move the frame (e. g. by damage, interaction, pistons, or missing supporting blocks), rotate the item or place/remove items.
13028.pattern:
item[ |-]frame %entities% (is|are) fixed
item[ |-]frame %entities% (isn't|is not|aren't|are not) fixed

13030.name: Projectile - has Left The Shooter
13030.desc:
Gets whether the provided projectiles have left the hitbox of their shooter and can now hit entities.
This is recalculated each tick if the projectile has a shooter.
13030.pattern:
%projectiles% (has|have) [already] left [the[ir]|its] shooter
%projectiles% (doesn't|does not|do not|don't) have [already] left [the[ir]|its] shooter

7399.name: Open Private Channel
7399.desc:
Opens a private channel with a specific user.
The opened channel can be null and an exception can be thrown if the user does not accept message.
7399.pattern: open [the] private (channel|message[s]) of [the] [member] %user% and store (it|the [private] channel) in %objects%

7911.name: Global variables stored on the Bungeecord
7911.desc: Set, get and delete a global variable stored on the Bungeecord. Value can be boolean, number or string.

12775.name: On Entity - Bat Toggle Sleep
12775.desc:
Called when a bat attempts to sleep or wake up from its slumber.
If a Bat Toggle Sleep event is cancelled, the Bat will not toggle its sleep state.
12775.pattern:
[on] bat [(state|mode)] toggle[d] sleep
[on] bat sleep [(state|mode)] toggle[d]

13287.name: On Log
13287.desc: This is called when a message is sent in console. Note that using broadcast on the on log event will infinitely loop.

12776.name: On Entity - Creeper Ignite
12776.desc: Called when a Creeper is ignited either by a flint and steel, Creeper.ignite() or Creeper.setIgnited(boolean).
12776.pattern:
[on] creeper ignite[d]
[on] creeper blow[n] up
[on] creeper explode[d]

13032.name: on Inventory Slot Drop - Drop Info
13032.desc: Checks if the item is being dropped from the cursor or the inventory, if the whole stack is being dropped or both.
13032.pattern:
[the] item is[( not|n't)] [being|getting] dropped from the (cursor|inventory)
[the] (whole|full) stack is[( not|n't)] [being|getting] dropped [from the (cursor|inventory)]

12777.name: On Entity - Dye
12777.desc: Called when an entity is dyed. Currently, this is called for org.bukkit.entity.Sheep being dyed, and org.bukkit.entity.Wolf/org.bukkit.entity.Cat collars being dyed
12777.eventvalues:
event-color
event-color
event-commandsender
event-entity
event-location
event-object
event-player
event-world

13033.name: Anvil GUI - Close
13033.desc:
Closes an anvil gui.
*NOTES*:
- Won't do anything if the anvil gui is not open.
- Must be used before opening another anvil gui for a player.

5354.name: SkDynmap - Description of area
5354.desc:
This expression returns the description of an area or an area builder.
You can use this expression to define the description of an area or an area builder.

6634.name: On Party Post Rename
6634.desc: Called when a player renamed a party. "event-partyplayer" can be null if executed by console.

13034.name: Anvil GUI - Open
13034.desc:
Opens an anvil GUI to one or more players.
*NOTES*:
- Anvil GUIs are always opened 1 tick later.
- You can only open an anvil GUI for a player if the player is not already viewing another (or this) anvil GUI.
- Using `force` will forcibly close the anvil GUI the player is currently viewing to open a new one. Be aware that, due to how anvil GUIs work, closing an anvil GUI is global, meaning it will be closed for all players viewing it. To avoid this, ensure that you create per-player anvil GUIs.

13035.name: Anvil GUI - Prevent Closing
13035.desc:
Prevents an anvil gui from closing.
*NOTES*:
- This effect must be used *BEFORE* the gui is opened; if you need to use it after it's already opened you'll have to open it again.
- If this effect is used you'll need to use the `Anvil GUI - Close` effect to close the gui.

6637.name: On Party Pre Rename
6637.desc: Called when a player is renaming a party. "event-partyplayer" can be null if executed by console. Cancellable.

7918.name: Server of bungee player
7918.desc: Get the server of a player on the network. NOTE: Server can be get only 2 ticks or more after the bungee player join event

13038.name: Ender Signal - Set Target Location Without Updating
13038.desc: Sets the location the provided ender signals are moving towards without changing the drop chance and the despawn timer.
13038.pattern:
set [the] ender (signal|eye) target location of %entities% to %location% without updating [it]
set %entities%'[s] ender (signal|eye) target location to %location% without updating [it]

5360.name: SkDynmap - Locations of area
5360.desc:
This expression returns the locations of an area or an area builder.
You can use this expression to define the locations of an area or an area builder.

10736.name: Files - Absolute file
10736.desc:
Return absolute file of file or directory
Like '/path to file/file' (path from root of machine filesystem)

12016.name: Shape Animation Ordering
12016.desc:
Controls the order in which the draw animation effect will draw points. Currently WIP, only supports 2 special orderings.
lowest-to-highest, which draws from -x -y -z to x y z, and the reverse.
12016.pattern: set the animation order of %shapes% to (default|1:lowest-to-highest|2:highest-to-lowest)

12784.name: On Entity - Enter Block
12784.desc:
Called when an Entity enters a block and is stored in that block.
This event is called for bees entering a bee hive. It is not called when a silverfish "enters" a stone block. For that listen to the EntityChangeBlockEvent.

5361.name: SkDynmap - Name of area
5361.desc:
This expression returns the world of an area or an area builder.
You can use this expression to define the world of an area or an area builder.

12785.name: On Entity - Enter Love Mode
12785.desc: Called when an entity enters love mode. This can be cancelled but the item will still be consumed that was used to make the entity enter into love mode.
12785.eventvalues:
event-commandsender
event-entity
event-livingentity
event-livingentity
event-location
event-player
event-world

13041.name: Entity Snapshot - Spawn
13041.desc:
Creates an entity using this template and spawns it at the provided location.
This is an effect, not a section and can't be used as such.
This effect is heavily influenced by Skript's Spawn effect (EffSecSpawn).

13297.name: On Citizen Damage
13297.desc:
Called when a Citizens NPC is damaged
Does not include damage by entity or damage by block, use their respective events for that.

13809.name: On Anvil GUI - on Anvil Gui Close
13809.desc:
Called when an Anvil Gui is opened.
*Note*:
- To cancel this event you'll need to use the `Anvil GUI - Prevent Closing` effect before this event is called.
13809.eventvalues:
event-anvil gui inventory
event-inventory
event-player
event-text
event-world

2546.name: Gamerule
2546.desc: The value (or default value) of the specified gamerule in the specified world. Gamerules whose syntaxes contain the word 'rule' are booleans, while all others are integers (as of Minecraft 1.13.2).
2546.pattern:
do tile drops rule [(default)] [in %world%]
do fire tick rule [(default)] [in %world%]
[(default)] max command chain length [in %world%]
reduced debug info rule [(default)] [in %world%]
natural regeneration rule [(default)] [in %world%]
disable elytra movement check rule [(default)] [in %world%]
do mob loot rule [(default)] [in %world%]
announce advancements rule [(default)] [in %world%]
keep inventory rule [(default)] [in %world%]
do entity drops rule [(default)] [in %world%]
do limited crafting rule [(default)] [in %world%]
mob griefing rule [(default)] [in %world%]
[(default)] random tick speed [in %world%]
command block output rule [(default)] [in %world%]
[(default)] spawn radius [in %world%]
do mob spawning rule [(default)] [in %world%]
[(default)] max entity cramming [in %world%]
log admin commands rule [(default)] [in %world%]
spectators generate chunks rule [(default)] [in %world%]
do weather cycle rule [(default)] [in %world%]
send command feedback rule [(default)] [in %world%]
do daylight cycle rule [(default)] [in %world%]
show death messages rule [(default)] [in %world%]

5362.name: SkDynmap - Name of area
5362.desc:
This expression returns the name of an area or an area builder.
You can use this expression to define the name of an area or an area builder.

12018.name: Helix Winding Rate
12018.desc:
Gets or sets the winding rate of a helix. The winding rate is the number of times the helix wraps around the axis per block.
The default winding rate is 1 loop per block, which delete or reset will set it to. The winding rate must be positive and non-zero.

12786.name: On Entity - Exhaustion
12786.desc: Called when a human entity experiences exhaustion. An exhaustion level greater than 4.0 causes a decrease in saturation by 1.

13042.name: Item Frame - Rotate
13042.desc: Rotates item frames counter clockwise and clockwise or by specific rotations and a set amount of times.

5363.name: SkDynmap - Style of area
5363.desc:
This expression returns the style of an area or an area builder.
You can use this expression to define the style of an area or an area builder.

12019.name: Shape Cutoff Angle
12019.desc:
The cutoff angle of a shape in degrees. This determines the portion of the whole shape that will be drawn in shapes like arcs and spherical caps. For example, a cutoff angle of 90 on an arc will create a quarter of a circle.
Note that an arc can range from 0 to 360 degrees, while a spherical cap can range from 0 to 180 degrees.

13811.name: On Block - on Damage Update
13811.desc:
Called when the progress of a block break is updated.
`event-number` = the block damage progress, ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, where 0 is no damage and 1.0 is the most damage.
13811.pattern:
[on] block damag(ing|e) update
[on] block break progress update

12020.name: Shape Length/Width/Height
12020.desc:
The length, width, or height of a shape. Changing this will change the size of the shape. Resetting or deleting it will set it back to the default value of 1.
Be sure to use 'shape length' instead of just 'length' to avoid conflicts with other syntax.

12788.name: On Entity - Fertilize Egg
12788.desc:
Called when two entities mate and the mating process results in a fertilization. Fertilization differs from normal breeding, as represented by the org.bukkit.event.entity.EntityBreedEvent, as it does not result in the immediate creation of the child entity in the world.
An example of this would be:
A frog being marked as "is_pregnant" and laying org.bukkit.Material.FROGSPAWN later.
Sniffers producing the org.bukkit.Material.SNIFFER_EGG item, which needs to be placed before it can begin to hatch.
A turtle being marked with "HasEgg" and laying a org.bukkit.Material.TURTLE_EGG later.
The event hence only exposes the two parent entities in the fertilization process and cannot provide the child entity, as it will only exist at a later point in time.
12788.eventvalues:
event-commandsender
event-entity
event-itemstack
event-location
event-player
event-world

13044.name: Player - Sleep
13044.desc:
Attempts to, or forces one or more players to sleep in a bed.
Attempting will fail under vanilla conditions in which the player cannot sleep, ex: Daytime, too far away, etc
13044.pattern:
(forcefully|(try|attempt) to) make %players% sleep at %location%
try making %players% sleep at %location%
force %players% to sleep at %location%

1013.name: Emotes - Built in
1013.desc: Using the names in the CustomEmotes.yml file you can play any custom emote or animation sequence you've made

12021.name: Shape Points
12021.desc:
Returns all the vectors from the center of the shape to the various points particles would be drawn at.
If you want the locations of the particles, it's advised use the 'shape locations' expression rather than doing it yourself.

Note that changing this property will not affect custom polygons, only regular polygons and polyhedrons.

12023.name: Shape Side Count - Polygonal/Polyhedral
12023.desc:

Changing this will change the number of sides of the shape accordingly, with a minimum of 3.
Note that custom polygons will return their side count, but will not be affected by this expression.
Polyhedrons will return their face count, and can only be set to 4, 8, 12, or 20.

Changing this will rotate the shape accordingly. Resetting or deleting it will set it back to the default orientation of (0, 0, 0, 1).
The expression returns a quaternion. You can use the quaternion and axis angle functions or the rotation expression to create an orientation.

12030.name: Shape Particle Density / Particle Count
12030.desc:
The density at which particles are spawned in a shape. This is in \"particles per meter\" (ppm), and defaults to 4.Be careful with this property, as it can cause lag if set to a high number. It's recommended to not go above 20 or so for this reason. 1000 ppm is the maximum value.
Keep in mind that this value scales with dimensions. A 1 meter line with a density of 20 will spawn 20 particles, but a 1 meter cube with a density of 20 will spawn 8,000 particles (2,400 if hollow).
Also, be aware that this may not be exact. Some shapes, like cuboids, will tweak the density a bit to ensure particles land exactly on the borders of the shape.

This syntax also supports setting the particle count directly, which is the amount of particles spawned in a shape.
Note that this is NOT exact. The actual amount of particles spawned will be the closest multiple of the particle count to the amount of particles needed to draw the shape.
For example, if the particle count of a solid cube is set to 100, the actual amount of particles spawned will be 125, which is the nearest cubic number.
The returned value of this expression will always be the accurate amount of particles spawned in a shape.

Changing this will change the particle density or count of the shape. Resetting or deleting it will set it back to the default density (4).

2562.name: Custom Generator
2562.desc:
Not an actual event, but rather an event-level scope used to code a custom generator, with the specified ID. Under the main "event" line you can have three different sub-scopes that handle generation:
initiation: This is called once at the beginning of a world's generation. This is specifically intended for optionally setting the world's spawn, but can also be used for other things you need to do at the start of generation.
generation: This is called whenever a chunk is being generated. All custom generators should use this to do their main generation of the world, using the given chunkdata to set the materials of the blocks in the chunk. Note that no block information beyond the material can be set during this stage. Any block state necessary beyond the material should be set during the population stage.
population: This is called after a chunk and all adjacent chunks (not including ones that are diagonal) have been generated, to add certain blocks on top which may require (or be made easier) by being able to put blocks on more than one chunk (ex. adding flowers). This stage should also be used if you need to specify blockdata in addition to the material.

10242.name: Rotate Shape

The axis can also be specified as a local or relative axis, which rotate relative to the shape's current rotation.
For example, you can rotate a shape around the global y axis, or around the shape's local y axis.
10242.pattern:
rotate shape[s] %shapes% around [relative:(relative|local)] (v:%-vector%|((:x|:y|:z)(-| )axis)) by %number% [degrees|:radians]
rotate shape[s] %shapes% (by|with) [rotation] %quaternion%

The first radius is the x radius, and the second is the y radius, and the last is the z radius. These are relative to the shape's rotation, so they only correspond exactly to the world axes if the shape is not rotated.
Note that this shape is modified using the Length/Width/Height modifiers, not the Radius modifier. This means the length/width/height of the shape will be twice the radius in each direction. Length is the x axis, width is the z axis, and height is the y axis.
NOTE: Very eccentric solid ellipsoids (those with a large difference between the radii) may have many more particles than expected. Be careful.

Note that the width and length are not exact, but they're roughly the width and length of the heart.
Finally, this shape does not support the particle count expression and its particle density is not uniform. If anyone knows a good way to compute the complete elliptic integral of the second kind, please let me know.
